They follow the same pattern: a private constructor, a validating static factory (Money.ofCents, Quantity.of), an add method, and ValidationError from DomainErrors for invalid input. Each rule lives in exactly one place. Money's rule (cents must be a non-negative whole number) is enforced only in Money.ofCents. Quantity's rule (a positive whole number) is enforced only in Quantity.of. The two rules are different, so the checks are not duplicates. Internal shortcuts are sound. Money.add and Quantity.add call the private constructor directly, which is safe because adding two valid values always gives a valid value. Money.multiply goes back through Money.ofCents, so a fractional or negative factor is still rejected. No file splits into an unrelated concern or bypasses the module's own abstractions.
